entries.name: Lesiba / gora
entries.description: A flattened quill converts forceful inhalation and exhalation into transverse string motion; the mouth selects harmonics from the sounding string.

entries.name: Harmonica
entries.description: Blow and draw pressure select opposing free reeds. The vocal tract feeds a strongly nonlinear, player-controlled acoustic load back to the reeds.

entries.name: Khaen
entries.description: A mouth chamber distributes inhaled or exhaled flow through bamboo pipes whose free reeds sound in either direction.

entries.name: Sheng
entries.description: Metal free reeds mounted in a wind chamber couple to tuned bamboo pipes and respond on both blown and drawn airflow.

entries.name: Shō
entries.description: Seventeen slender pipes form sustained aitake tone clusters, maintained through alternating outward and inward breath.

entries.name: Hulusi
entries.description: Exhaled air enters a gourd wind chest and drives a melody-pipe free reed plus one or more drone pipes.

entries.name: Bawu
entries.description: A side-blown bamboo pipe uses an enclosed free reed as its pressure valve, with finger holes setting the air-column resonance.

entries.name: Didgeridoo / yidaki
entries.description: Exhaled pressure opens and closes the lips against a long irregular bore while the player's vocal-tract impedance sculpts its spectral peaks.

entries.name: Pungi / been

entries.name: Nose flute

entries.name: Overtone flute

entries.name: ʻUkeke

entries.name: Umrhubhe

entries.name: Lunku mouth bow
entries.description: A twanged string supplies a harmonic spectrum while the bow is pressed to the mouth, turning the oral cavity into its resonator.

entries.name: Berimbau-de-boca
entries.description: Unlike the gourd-resonated capoeira berimbau, this mouth-bow form couples its plucked string directly to a changing oral resonator.

entries.name: K’ni
entries.description: A bowed string sends vibration along a cord held at the mouth; the player's oral cavity becomes a highly articulate remote resonator.

entries.name: Makomako jaw harp

entries.name: Mukkuri

entries.name: Đàn môi
entries.description: A light brass lamella rests against the lips rather than the teeth; pluck, signed airflow, and oral articulation all strongly affect its sound.
